reference: Native @google/adk 2.3.0 browser bundle (dist/web/index_web.js) driven by its own Runner, run on Node
normalizations: Function-call and function-response IDs are runtime-generated on each side (ADK uses adk-<uuid>, galaxie uses galaxie-<n>), so transcripts compare names and payloads only.

Requests are recorded at the ADK model boundary on both sides: the scripted BaseLlm on the native side and a wrapper around host.adk.llm(role) on the galaxie side. The galaxie scripted replies come from the deterministic mock chat model behind the router.

Run errors compare by code. ADK reports a failed run as an error event whose code is UNKNOWN_ERROR or INVOCATION_ABORTED; the native harness maps its call-limit message to budget_exceeded, an aborted invocation to cancelled, and its own host-check emulation to denied.

The native lane emulates the host output-safety hook with the same BLOCKED_ pattern the galaxie run uses; the native lane has no router, so this stands in for the host hook only to keep the case comparable.
A request that galaxie's step budget refuses before dispatch is dropped from the galaxie transcript, because ADK's call limit refuses before it asks the model.
limits: Stage A2 is non-streaming, with no interrupts, resume, checkpoints or subgraphs. The adapter reports every optional feature as false.
The run input is { prompt: string }. Only the closed set of LlmAgent, SequentialAgent, ParallelAgent and LoopAgent is accepted, and tools and models must come from the host.
All model replies are deterministic scripts; no real model, network request or download takes part.
The Chromium lane runs under the vitest browser project, not a page with the strict mock CSP; the strict-CSP bundle probe in packages/adapter-adk covers the bundle alone.
